## Before you start

This is Part 2 of [Friendly Introduction to Agentic AI for Social Scientists](index.qmd). It assumes you have finished [Part 1 — Setup](setup.qmd): the app works, `first-project` is open in the Code tab in **Manual** mode, Python is set up, and Typora opens `.md` files.

It takes about an hour.

::: {.callout-note}
## What you will have at the end

- ☐ A routine for working on Word documents, with every change visible as a tracked change
- ☐ An `AGENTS.md` file with standing instructions for the agent
- ☐ Two **skills**: one to log analytical decisions, one to read PDFs reliably
- ☐ One small, real analysis, with numbers you checked yourself
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Step 2.1 — Working on Word documents

Most of your writing, and your coauthors', lives in Word. The agent can read, comment on, edit and create Word files. The routine below keeps you in control: **the agent never touches your original, and you see each change as a tracked change in Word.**

**Get ready.** Copy a Word document you know well (a draft, a proposal, a referee report) into a `docs/` subfolder. Pick one that is not confidential.

### Ask for comments, not changes

The safest start: nothing is edited.

``` text
Read docs/draft.docx. Do not change it.
Give me the ten most important comments on the argument, structure and
clarity, most important first. For each, say which section or paragraph
it refers to. Save the list as docs/draft_comments.md.
```

Open the list in Typora. Some comments will be useful, some generic, a few wrong. That mix tells you a lot about how to use the agent.

### Ask for edits, then review them as tracked changes

``` text
Make a copy of docs/draft.docx called docs/draft_v2.docx. In the copy only:
fix grammar and typos, and split sentences longer than 40 words.
Do not change the argument, the citations or the numbers.
Keep all formatting, footnotes and comments.
When done, list the kinds of changes you made.
```

Then let Word show what changed:

1. In desktop Word (the browser version cannot compare), go to the **Review** tab, click **Compare**, then **Compare…** (Windows) or **Compare Documents** (Mac).
2. As *Original document*, choose `draft.docx`. As *Revised document*, choose `draft_v2.docx`.
3. Word opens a new document with each change as a **tracked change**. Accept or reject them as you would a coauthor's.

There is nothing new to learn, and it shows any change you did not ask for.

### Write in Markdown, finish in Word

For new text (a memo, a section, a report), draft and revise in Markdown with the agent, and convert to Word at the end. The agent works best in plain text, and its changes are easier to follow there.

``` text
Convert docs/memo.md to docs/memo.docx.
Use docs/my-template.docx for the styles (fonts, headings, margins).
```

For `my-template.docx`, use any Word file whose look you like (your university template, a past paper). The agent copies its styles, not its text.

### Margin comments

You can also ask: *"Put your comments as Word comments in the margin of docs/draft_v2.docx."* This usually works. If the result looks odd, use the list in Markdown instead.

## Step 2.2 — Give the agent standing instructions: AGENTS.md

Each session starts from zero: the agent does not remember yesterday. So write down once what it should always know: who you are, how you work, what it must never do. This file, **`AGENTS.md`**, sits in the project folder, and the agent reads it at the start of every session.

We prepared a starter file based on how we work with agents. Ask the agent to fetch it and create the folders:

``` text
Download this file exactly (use a download command, do not retype it) and
save it as AGENTS.md in this folder:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabors-data-analysis/da-w-ai/main/friendly-agentic-ai-intro/starter/AGENTS.md

Then create the folders it describes (data/raw, data/clean, code, output, docs)
and summarize the instructions for me in five bullet points.
```

Then open `AGENTS.md` in Typora and **edit the "About me" section**. It is your file.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## What is in the starter AGENTS.md (click to open)

```` markdown
{{< include starter/AGENTS.md >}}
````
:::

In short, it says: plan before longer tasks; do the smallest thing that answers the request; never delete (move files to `_old/`); never overwrite raw data or your Word files; never invent numbers or references; say where each number comes from; check results by hand; log analytical decisions.

Grow the file slowly. **When the agent makes the same mistake twice, add one line.** After a month it will fit how you work better than any template.

## Step 2.3 — Add two skills

A **skill** is a recipe for one type of task: a Markdown file called `SKILL.md` in its own folder. The agent uses a skill when the task matches its description, or when you type `/` and its name.

Two to start with:

- **`decision-log`** records every analytical choice in `DECISIONS.md`: dropped observations, variable definitions, methods. For each, it notes the alternatives and the basis (evidence, convention, your instruction, or just a default). Read it *before* you trust the results.
- **`read-pdf`** makes the agent extract a PDF's text to a `.txt` file first and work from that, citing page numbers. This prevents the most common PDF failure: answering from a partly read document without saying so.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## The decision-log skill (click to open)

```` markdown
{{< include starter/skills/decision-log/SKILL.md >}}
````
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## The read-pdf skill (click to open)

```` markdown
{{< include starter/skills/read-pdf/SKILL.md >}}
````
:::

Install them with this prompt:

``` text
Download these two files exactly (use a download command, do not retype them):
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabors-data-analysis/da-w-ai/main/friendly-agentic-ai-intro/starter/skills/decision-log/SKILL.md
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabors-data-analysis/da-w-ai/main/friendly-agentic-ai-intro/starter/skills/read-pdf/SKILL.md

Save them as .claude/skills/decision-log/SKILL.md and
.claude/skills/read-pdf/SKILL.md inside this project folder.
Then tell me in two sentences what each skill does.
```

Folders starting with a dot, like `.claude`, are hidden by default, so you may not see it in Explorer or Finder. Start a new session (**+** or *New session*) and type `/`: both skills should show up.

**Try the PDF skill** on a paper you know well: *"Use the read-pdf skill on [file name]. What is the research question, the data, the main result? Give page numbers."* Check one page number yourself. Then ask *"What are the three weakest points of this paper?"* and judge the answer as a referee would.

## Step 2.4 — A first real task with data

Now it all comes together. Start a new session and, before you send the prompt, switch the permission mode to **Plan**. In Plan mode the agent proposes but changes nothing until you agree.

``` text
Using the World Bank's open data (its API, no key needed), get for all
EU countries for 2023:
- female labour force participation rate (% of women 15+)
- GDP per capita, PPP

Save the raw download in data/raw, write the code in code/, and make
one scatter plot (GDP per capita on the x axis, participation on the y axis,
with country labels) saved in output/. Then write a half-page memo in
docs/memo.md: what the chart shows, and three caveats.
Keep the decision log as you go.
```

Read the plan, and say plainly if something looks off. When you are happy, switch back to **Manual** and tell it to go ahead.

**Then check it. This is your job, not the agent's.**

1. Open the chart. Are the countries where you expected?
2. Pick **two countries** and look up their numbers on [data.worldbank.org](https://data.worldbank.org/). Do they match the CSV?
3. Read `DECISIONS.md`. Which countries had no 2023 data, and what did the agent do: use another year, drop them, or ask you?
4. Read the memo. Does it say "effect" or "causes"? It shouldn't: a cross-country scatter shows an association.

If you find a mistake, tell the agent, and add a line to `AGENTS.md` if it could happen again. Finally, ask for the memo as a Word file (Step 2.1).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Habits that make it work

None of these is technical.

1. **Plan first.** For anything longer than a few minutes, use Plan mode. Fixing a plan costs a sentence; fixing finished work costs an afternoon.
2. **Small steps.** Ask for one thing, check it, then ask for the next. An agent running on a vague task produces plausible-looking work that you then have to read.
3. **Check the numbers.** Compare a few values with the source by hand, every time. A smaller result you checked beats a larger one you did not.
4. **Never let it delete or overwrite.** Raw data and original documents stay untouched; old files go to `_old/`. Then every mistake can be undone.
5. **One session per task.** Long sessions get muddled. Start a new one for each task; what must carry over goes in `AGENTS.md`, `DECISIONS.md` or a notes file.
6. **Ask it to explain.** "Why did you do that?" "What could go wrong here?" You are responsible for the work, so you need to understand it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | What to do |
|---|---|
| Word Compare shows changes everywhere | The agent probably rebuilt the whole document. Ask it to start again from a fresh copy and change only the text |
| The skills don't show up when I type `/` | Start a new session. Skills load when a session starts |
| The agent seems stuck, or keeps doing the wrong thing | Click stop and say plainly what you want. If the session is long, start a new one |
| It made a mess of my files | Ask: *"List every file you created or changed in this session."* Then ask it to move the unwanted ones to `_old/` |
| An error I don't understand | Paste it in and ask: *"Explain this error simply, then fix it."* |

More setup problems: [Part 1](setup.qmd#troubleshooting). Unfamiliar terms: the [glossary](index.qmd#a-short-glossary) on the course page.
